title: Time-weighted billing smoothing & ephemeral credits for cross-cycle spikes
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Problem: Enterprise customers have raised a recurring support pattern where short-lived usage spikes (bursts from load tests, seasonal jobs, or tokenizer edge cases) that straddle a month boundary generate large overage charges for a single billing cycle even though the customer's long-run usage is within committed capacity. This is particularly painful during contract renewals and security questionnaire reviews where finance and procurement highlight one-off overages as a risk. Proposal: run a controlled experiment to introduce a time-weighted smoothing mechanism and an ephemeral crediting policy that (1) detects cross-cycle spikes caused by transient bursts, (2) attributes excess token usage proportionally across adjacent cycles (time-weighted), and (3) auto-applies an ephemeral credit for the affected invoice with clear audit trail and customer notification. Goals: reduce disputed invoices and manual adjustments, preserve fiscal integrity of metering, and avoid opening the door to gaming. This ticket defines acceptance criteria, the experimental rollout path, observability/alerts needed, and the decision criteria to promote the behavior to production or revert it. Key constraints: must not change per-token pricing or long-run accounting; credits must be transparent and reversible; QA must verify no double-crediting with reserved capacity burst allowances.
acceptance_criteria: S1: Smoothing algorithm correctly detects transient spikes that begin within 48 hours of the month boundary and last less than 72 hours (configurable).
S2: Time-weighted attribution splits excess tokens across adjacent cycles based on per-minute usage weight and updates provisional invoice preview within 24 hours of detection.
S3: Ephemeral credit auto-applies to the next invoice with audit metadata (reason, trigger window, detection score, operator id) and appears in billing dashboard and invoice PDF/descriptions.

S4: No customer sees net lower invoice than what their contract would permit for sustained over-usage; smoothing only addresses transient spikes (false positive rate < 1% measured on historical dataset).
S5: Support flow and resolution runbook created and validated with CS; disputed invoices where smoothing applied are flagged automatically for quicker review.
